## Load packages

`GO.db`, `AnnotationDbi`, `eulerr` and `enrichVolcano` (the user's own package, not on CRAN) are
called with `::` for one job each.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, patchwork, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/07_leading_edge/a_script/07_leading_edge.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

The question: for pathways both legs move the same way with training, do the same proteins drive
them? The comparison uses fgsea leading edges. In gene set enrichment, proteins are ranked by
their training statistic and a running sum walks down the ranking, rising at each set member; the
leading edge is the set members ranked before the running sum peaks, the ones carrying the
enrichment. This step reads the fgsea run `01_run_fgsea_and_fry` already made, so nothing is
re-ranked. Adapted from Sam's PR #26 (sc-norton): his overlap measures, GO hierarchy breakdown
and unique-protein split, on the pipeline's fgsea results and gene sets.

Inputs: the `set_tests` and `protein_results` sheets from `01_run_fgsea_and_fry` (one row per set,
method and contrast, leading edges as `;`-joined symbols; one row per protein and contrast, with
its t), and from `00_build_gene_sets` the set catalogue and the measured genes of every GO:BP set.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "07_leading_edge")
fgsea_book <- here(
  "03_Pathway_Enrichment", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry", "c_data", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx"
)
set_tests <- read_excel(fgsea_book, "set_tests")
protein_results <- read_excel(fgsea_book, "protein_results")
set_catalog <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"),
  "set_catalog"
)
go_sets <- readRDS(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "go_bp_measured.rds")
)
arms <- c(BFR = "BFR_Post-Pre", HLRT = "HLRT_Post-Pre")
arm_colours <- c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC")
dim(set_tests)
```

## Select the shared pathways

Keep the fgsea rows for the two training contrasts, one per leg. A pathway is kept when fgsea
calls it at FDR < 0.05 in both legs, with the same sign of NES (normalised enrichment score, the
direction and strength of the enrichment), and when it is a main set after `collapsePathways` in
at least one leg, so one representative stands for each cluster of overlapping sets.

```{r shared-sets}
fgsea <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% arms) |>
  mutate(arm = names(arms)[match(contrast, arms)]) |>
  select(set_id, database, pathway, n, arm, NES, padj, main, leadingEdge)
shared_sets <- fgsea |>
  summarise(
    keep = all(padj < 0.05) && n_distinct(sign(NES)) == 1 && any(main), .by = set_id
  ) |>
  filter(keep) |>
  pull(set_id)
length(shared_sets)
```

## Compare the leading edges

Split each kept pathway's leading edges into one row per protein, then record which legs list
that protein: BFR only, HLRT only or both.

```{r proteins}
proteins <- fgsea |>
  filter(set_id %in% shared_sets) |>
  separate_longer_delim(leadingEdge, ";") |>
  rename(gene = leadingEdge) |>
  summarise(
    in_arm = paste(sort(arm), collapse = " and "), .by = c(set_id, database, pathway, gene)
  ) |>
  mutate(in_arm = recode(in_arm, "BFR and HLRT" = "both"))
head(proteins, 4)
```

Count the three groups per pathway and add Sam's three overlap measures:

- Jaccard index, proteins in both leading edges over proteins in either: 1 when the legs share
  every driver, 0 when they share none;
- overlap coefficient, proteins in both over the smaller leading edge: 1 when one leg's edge sits
  inside the other's;
- `expected_shared`, the proteins two leading edges of these sizes would share if each were a
  random draw from the pathway's `n` measured members.

Each leg's NES and adjusted p ride along, and rows sort from the lowest Jaccard index.

```{r leading-edge}
leading_edge <- proteins |>
  count(set_id, database, pathway, in_arm) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = in_arm, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(
    fgsea |>
      select(set_id, n, arm, NES, padj) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(NES, padj)),
    by = "set_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    jaccard = both / (both + BFR + HLRT),
    overlap_coef = both / pmin(both + BFR, both + HLRT),
    expected_shared = (both + BFR) * (both + HLRT) / n
  ) |>
  arrange(jaccard) |>
  mutate(label = enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 1000))
head(select(leading_edge, label, both, expected_shared, BFR, HLRT, jaccard), 6)
```

Leading edges shift with small changes in the ranking, so these overlaps describe and do not
test.

## Break GO:BP parents into children

Sam's GO hierarchy view, for each GO:BP pathway both legs move. `GO.db::GOBPCHILDREN` gives a
parent's direct child terms, each with its relation (`isa`, `part_of`, `regulates`). A child's
genes are its measured MSigDB members inside the parent's measured members, which form the
universe, and a child needs at least three of them, as in Sam's code. `mget()` returns `NA` for a
term without children.

```{r go-children}
go_ids <- filter(set_catalog, database == "GOBP") |> select(set_id, source_id)
parents <- inner_join(filter(leading_edge, database == "GOBP"), go_ids, by = "set_id")
children_of <- AnnotationDbi::mget(parents$source_id, GO.db::GOBPCHILDREN, ifnotfound = NA)
go_children <- parents |>
  transmute(parent_id = set_id, parent = label, kids = map(source_id, function(id) {
    kids <- children_of[[id]][!is.na(children_of[[id]])]
    tibble(child_go = as.character(kids), relation = names(kids) %||% character())
  })) |>
  unnest(kids) |>
  summarise(relation = str_flatten(unique(relation), ","), .by = c(parent_id, parent, child_go)) |>
  inner_join(rename(go_ids, child_id = set_id, child_go = source_id), by = "child_go") |>
  mutate(
    child = enrichVolcano::clean_label(
      set_catalog$pathway[match(child_id, set_catalog$set_id)], width = 1000
    ),
    members = map2(go_sets[child_id], go_sets[parent_id], intersect)
  ) |>
  filter(lengths(members) >= 3)
c(parents = nrow(parents), children = nrow(go_children))
```

`edge()` returns a parent's leading-edge proteins in one leg, inside the parent's measured
members.

```{r edge}
edge <- function(id, which_arm) {
  intersect(
    filter(proteins, set_id == id, in_arm %in% c(which_arm, "both"))$gene, go_sets[[id]]
  )
}
```

For every parent, child and leg, Sam's decomposition counts the parent's leading-edge proteins in
the child, as a share of the leading edge and as a fold over the child's share of the universe,
with a one-sided hypergeometric p for concentration in that child, BH within parent and leg.
Children overlap and the tests are nested on small sets, so the p values describe.

```{r decomposition}
decomposition <- go_children |>
  cross_join(tibble(arm = names(arms))) |>
  mutate(
    core = map2(parent_id, arm, edge),
    universe = lengths(go_sets[parent_id]), child_size = lengths(members),
    core_size = lengths(core), in_child = map2_int(core, members, function(x, y) {
      length(intersect(x, y))
    }),
    share_of_edge = in_child / core_size,
    fold = share_of_edge / (child_size / universe),
    p = phyper(in_child - 1, child_size, universe - child_size, core_size, lower.tail = FALSE),
    genes = map2_chr(core, members, function(x, y) str_flatten(sort(intersect(x, y)), ";"))
  ) |>
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(p, "BH"), .by = c(parent_id, arm)) |>
  select(-core, -members)
head(select(decomposition, parent, child, arm, in_child, share_of_edge, padj), 6)
```

Sam's coverage check asks the reverse: what share of a parent's leading edge already sits in the
leading edges of its significant descendants (any depth, `GOBPOFFSPRING`, tested sets at FDR < 0.05
in the same leg). A low share means the parent carries signal no more specific term captures;
`unexplained` lists those proteins.

```{r coverage}
offspring_of <- AnnotationDbi::mget(parents$source_id, GO.db::GOBPOFFSPRING, ifnotfound = NA)
significant <- fgsea |>
  filter(database == "GOBP", padj < 0.05) |>
  inner_join(go_ids, by = "set_id")
go_coverage <- parents |>
  select(parent_id = set_id, parent = label, source_id) |>
  cross_join(tibble(arm = names(arms))) |>
  mutate(
    core = map2(parent_id, arm, edge),
    descendants = map2(source_id, arm, function(id, which_arm) {
      filter(significant, arm == which_arm, source_id %in% offspring_of[[id]])
    }),
    significant_descendants = map_int(descendants, nrow),
    covered = map(descendants, function(d) unique(unlist(str_split(d$leadingEdge, ";")))),
    explained = map2_dbl(core, covered, function(x, y) mean(x %in% y)),
    unexplained = map2_chr(core, covered, function(x, y) str_flatten(sort(setdiff(x, y)), ";"))
  ) |>
  select(parent_id, parent, arm, significant_descendants, explained, unexplained)
summary(go_coverage$explained)
```

## Split the unique proteins

Sam's last view takes the proteins in one leg's leading edge only (BFR-only and HLRT-only) and asks
whether the two groups fall in different children. Per child, Fisher's exact test compares the
share of BFR-only and HLRT-only proteins in it, BH within parent. Per parent, the divergence sums
the absolute share differences over children plus a "(no child term)" bin, and its p comes from
2,000 shuffles of the BFR and HLRT labels among the unique proteins, BH across parents. Both tests
treat proteins as exchangeable, which co-regulated proteins are not, so they describe.
`edge_pct` is the median position of each leg's unique proteins in the other leg's ranking,
measured from the enriched end: near 0 means they only just missed the other leading edge. A parent
needs at least three unique proteins in each leg, as in Sam's code.

```{r unique-children}
rank_position <- protein_results |>
  filter(selected, contrast %in% arms) |>
  mutate(arm = names(arms)[match(contrast, arms)], position = rank(-t) / n(), .by = contrast) |>
  select(arm, gene, position)
edge_pct <- function(genes, which_arm, nes) {
  position <- filter(rank_position, arm == which_arm, gene %in% genes)$position
  median(if (nes < 0) 1 - position else position)
}
set.seed(1)
unique_children <- parents |>
  pmap(function(set_id, label, NES_BFR, NES_HLRT, ...) {
    only <- map(set_names(names(arms)), function(a) {
      intersect(filter(proteins, set_id == !!set_id, in_arm == a)$gene, go_sets[[set_id]])
    })
    kids <- filter(go_children, parent_id == set_id)
    if (min(lengths(only)) < 3 || nrow(kids) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    genes <- c(only$BFR, only$HLRT)
    is_bfr <- seq_along(genes) <= length(only$BFR)
    in_child <- matrix(sapply(kids$members, function(m) genes %in% m), nrow = length(genes))
    in_child <- cbind(in_child, rowSums(in_child) == 0)
    divergence <- function(bfr) {
      sum(abs(colMeans(in_child[bfr, , drop = FALSE]) - colMeans(in_child[!bfr, , drop = FALSE])))
    }
    observed <- divergence(is_bfr)
    shuffled <- replicate(2000, divergence(sample(is_bfr)))
    tibble(
      parent_id = set_id, parent = label, child = c(kids$child, "(no child term)"),
      only_BFR = length(only$BFR), only_HLRT = length(only$HLRT),
      shared = sum(filter(proteins, set_id == !!set_id)$in_arm == "both"),
      BFR_in_child = colSums(in_child[is_bfr, , drop = FALSE]),
      HLRT_in_child = colSums(in_child[!is_bfr, , drop = FALSE]),
      p = map2_dbl(BFR_in_child, HLRT_in_child, function(b, h) {
        fisher.test(matrix(c(b, length(only$BFR) - b, h, length(only$HLRT) - h), 2))$p.value
      }),
      divergence = observed, p_divergence = (1 + sum(shuffled >= observed - 1e-12)) / 2001,
      BFR_only_pct_in_HLRT = edge_pct(only$BFR, "HLRT", NES_HLRT),
      HLRT_only_pct_in_BFR = edge_pct(only$HLRT, "BFR", NES_BFR)
    ) |>
      mutate(padj = p.adjust(p, "BH"))
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(padj_divergence = p.adjust(p_divergence[!duplicated(parent_id)], "BH")[
    match(parent_id, unique(parent_id))
  ])
distinct(unique_children, parent, only_BFR, only_HLRT, shared, divergence, padj_divergence) |>
  arrange(padj_divergence) |>
  head()
```

## Draw figures

All pages share a caption style, with captions wrapped at 115 characters.

```{r page-style}
page_theme <- theme(
  plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
  plot.caption.position = "plot"
)
```

S20 puts every shared pathway on one page: a bar per pathway split into proteins in both leading
edges and in one leg only, lowest overlap at the bottom of each collection.

```{r overlap-page}
overlap_page <- leading_edge |>
  mutate(label = factor(str_trunc(label, 60), unique(str_trunc(label, 60)))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(both, BFR, HLRT), names_to = "in_arm", values_to = "proteins") |>
  mutate(in_arm = factor(in_arm, c("BFR", "both", "HLRT"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(proteins, label, fill = in_arm)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  facet_grid(database ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(BFR = "#B2182B", both = "grey55", HLRT = "#2166AC"), name = "leading edge in"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "leading-edge proteins", y = NULL,
    caption = str_wrap(paste(
      "S20 Figure. Leading-edge overlap between the legs. Every pathway that fgsea calls at FDR",
      sprintf("< 0.05 in both training contrasts, in the same direction (%d,", nrow(leading_edge)),
      "each a main set after collapse in at least one leg). Bars split each pathway's",
      "leading-edge proteins into those shared by both legs and those in one leg only; lowest",
      "overlap at the bottom of each collection. The leading_edge sheet adds the Jaccard index,",
      "the overlap coefficient and the shared count expected by chance. Leading edges move with",
      "small ranking changes, so this describes and does not test. Data: leading_edge sheet of",
      "07_leading_edge.xlsx."
    ), 115)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6), strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
    legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  page_theme
```

S21 is Sam's Venn view: one Venn diagram per pathway, circle areas proportional to the counts
(`eulerr` fits them), with each leg's NES and adjusted p (q), the shared count against chance,
and the shared proteins named beneath, six to a page. `venn()` takes a set ID and returns that
pathway's panel. `euler()` starts its layout search from random positions, so the seed keeps the
drawing the same between renders.

```{r venn-pages}
set.seed(1)
venn <- function(id) {
  counts <- filter(leading_edge, set_id == id)
  fit <- eulerr::euler(c(BFR = counts$BFR, HLRT = counts$HLRT, "BFR&HLRT" = counts$both))
  shared <- sort(filter(proteins, set_id == id, in_arm == "both")$gene)
  wrap_elements(full = plot(
    fit,
    fills = list(fill = arm_colours, alpha = 0.6), quantities = list(fontsize = 8),
    labels = list(fontsize = 8)
  )) +
    labs(
      title = str_wrap(counts$label, 45),
      subtitle = paste0(
        sprintf(
          "NES %.2f BFR, %.2f HLRT; q %.2g, %.2g; shared %d, expected %.1f\n",
          counts$NES_BFR, counts$NES_HLRT, counts$padj_BFR, counts$padj_HLRT, counts$both,
          counts$expected_shared
        ),
        str_wrap(paste(shared, collapse = " "), 70)
      )
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 5, lineheight = 1.1)
    )
}
venn_pages <- split(leading_edge$set_id, ceiling(seq_along(leading_edge$set_id) / 6)) |>
  imap(function(ids, page) {
    wrap_plots(map(ids, venn), ncol = 2) +
      plot_annotation(caption = str_wrap(sprintf(paste(
        "S21 Figure (page %s of %d). Leading edges by leg, one Venn per pathway in the order of",
        "S20. Areas follow the counts of proteins in each leg's leading edge only and in both.",
        "Under each title: NES and BH-adjusted p (q) per leg, the shared count against the count",
        "two random leading edges of the same sizes would share, and the shared proteins. Data:",
        "leading_edge and proteins sheets of 07_leading_edge.xlsx."
      ), page, ceiling(nrow(leading_edge) / 6)), 115), theme = page_theme)
  })
```

S22 is Sam's decomposition plot, six parents to a page: one row per child term (up to 15 per
parent, those holding the largest share of either leg's leading edge), one column per leg. Fill is
the share of the parent's leading edge in the child, size the count, and a black outline marks a
child at BH-adjusted p < 0.05. Each panel title carries the coverage share per leg.

```{r child-pages}
coverage_label <- go_coverage |>
  select(parent_id, arm, explained) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = explained) |>
  transmute(
    parent_id, panel = sprintf("explained BFR %.0f%%, HLRT %.0f%%", 100 * BFR, 100 * HLRT)
  )
child_pages <- decomposition |>
  filter(max(in_child) > 0, .by = c(parent_id, child_id)) |>
  filter(child_id %in% unique(child_id[order(-share_of_edge)])[1:15], .by = parent_id) |>
  left_join(coverage_label, by = "parent_id") |>
  mutate(
    panel = paste0(str_wrap(parent, 38), "\n", panel),
    child = str_trunc(sprintf("%s [%s]", child, relation), 55),
    significant = factor(padj < 0.05, c(TRUE, FALSE)),
    page = ceiling(match(parent_id, unique(parent_id)) / 6)
  ) |>
  split(~page) |>
  imap(function(rows, page) {
    ggplot(rows, aes(arm, reorder(child, share_of_edge))) +
      geom_point(
        aes(size = in_child, fill = share_of_edge, colour = significant),
        shape = 21, stroke = 0.7
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#f7fbff", high = "#08519c", limits = c(0, 1), name = "share of\nleading edge"
      ) +
      scale_colour_manual(
        values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "grey75"), labels = c("q < 0.05", "n.s."),
        drop = FALSE, name = "child test"
      ) +
      scale_size_area(max_size = 5, name = "proteins") +
      labs(
        x = NULL, y = NULL,
        caption = str_wrap(sprintf(paste(
          "S22 Figure (page %s of %d). GO:BP pathways both legs move, broken into their direct",
          "child terms [relation] with at least three measured proteins. Fill is the share of the",
          "parent's leading edge in the child, size the protein count; a black outline marks a",
          "one-sided hypergeometric p below 0.05 after BH within parent and leg. Children overlap",
          "and the tests are nested, so they describe. Panel titles give the share of each leg's",
          "leading edge already in significant descendant terms. Data: go_children and",
          "go_coverage sheets of 07_leading_edge.xlsx."
        ), page, ceiling(n_distinct(decomposition$parent_id) / 6)), 115)
      ) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 7) +
      theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 6), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
      page_theme
  })
```

S23 is Sam's unique-protein view, four parents to a page in order of the divergence p: per child,
BFR-only proteins to the left and HLRT-only to the right (up to 15 children, the most populated),
with the shared count in brackets and an asterisk at Fisher BH p < 0.05.

```{r unique-pages}
unique_pages <- unique_children |>
  filter(BFR_in_child + HLRT_in_child > 0) |>
  slice_max(BFR_in_child + HLRT_in_child, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE, by = parent_id) |>
  arrange(p_divergence) |>
  mutate(
    panel = sprintf(
      "%s\nonly BFR %d, only HLRT %d, shared %d; divergence %.2f, p %.3g (BH %.3g)",
      str_wrap(parent, 50), only_BFR, only_HLRT, shared, divergence, p_divergence,
      padj_divergence
    ),
    panel = factor(panel, unique(panel)),
    child = str_trunc(paste0(if_else(padj < 0.05, "* ", ""), child), 50),
    page = ceiling(as.integer(panel) / 4)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(BFR_in_child, HLRT_in_child), names_to = "arm", values_to = "proteins") |>
  mutate(
    arm = sub("_in_child", "", arm), proteins = if_else(arm == "BFR", -proteins, proteins)
  ) |>
  split(~page) |>
  imap(function(rows, page) {
    ggplot(rows, aes(proteins, reorder(child, proteins), fill = arm)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
      facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = abs) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = arm_colours, name = "proteins unique to") +
      labs(
        x = "unique leading-edge proteins in the child term", y = NULL,
        caption = str_wrap(sprintf(paste(
          "S23 Figure (page %s of %d). Proteins in one leg's leading edge only, by child term, for",
          "GO:BP parents with at least three such proteins in each leg; BFR-only to the left,",
          "HLRT-only to the right. Panel titles give the counts and the divergence between the",
          "two groups' child profiles, with p from 2,000 label shuffles (BH across parents); an",
          "asterisk marks a child at Fisher BH p < 0.05. Both tests treat proteins as",
          "exchangeable, so they describe. Children overlap. Data: unique_children sheet of",
          "07_leading_edge.xlsx."
        ), page, ceiling(n_distinct(unique_children$parent_id) / 4)), 115)
      ) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 7) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      ) +
      page_theme
  })
```

All pages go to one A4 PDF, S20 first.

```{r write-figures}
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "07_leading_edge.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
walk(c(list(overlap_page), venn_pages, child_pages, unique_pages), print)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Summary

Shared pathways per collection, the spread of the Jaccard index and of the shared count over
chance, the GO:BP breakdown, and the parents whose unique proteins split most clearly.

```{r summary}
count(leading_edge, database)
summary(leading_edge$jaccard)
summary(leading_edge$both / leading_edge$expected_shared)
c(
  parents = n_distinct(decomposition$parent_id),
  children = n_distinct(decomposition$child_id),
  parents_split = n_distinct(unique_children$parent_id)
)
group_by(go_coverage, arm) |>
  summarise(median_explained = median(explained))
distinct(unique_children, parent, padj_divergence) |>
  filter(padj_divergence < 0.05)
```

## Save results

`07_leading_edge.xlsx` holds `leading_edge` (one row per pathway), `proteins` (one row per
pathway and leading-edge protein), `go_children` (one row per parent, child and leg),
`go_coverage` (one row per parent and leg) and `unique_children` (one row per parent and child).

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  leading_edge = leading_edge, proteins = proteins, go_children = decomposition,
  go_coverage = go_coverage, unique_children = unique_children
)
write_xlsx(sheets, file.path(stage, "c_data", "07_leading_edge.xlsx"))
```
